message.content:
During the nineteenth‑century boom in modern sculpture, **Auguste Rodin’s “The Thinker”** emerged as arguably the single most renowned work of its time.  
* Originally conceived in 1877–78 as part of his monumental project *Gates of Hell*, it later received independent acclaim after being cast separately around 1902.  
* Its dramatic pose—an adult male hunched over in deep contemplation—captured both the Romantic fascination with individual emotion and the emerging Modernist interest in psychological depth.  

While many masterpieces were produced throughout the century—from Antonio Canova’s neoclassical figures to Jean-Baptiste Carpeaux’s dynamic bronze groups—the widespread reproduction, critical discussion, and enduring public presence of *The Thinker* made it the emblematic sculpture of the age.
